candidates.topic: Tarrare — The Man Who Ate Everything
candidates.teaser: A French soldier in the 1700s had a hunger so extreme that doctors suspected he ate a living infant — and they couldn't prove he didn't.
candidates.video_title: The Man Whose Hunger Had No Limit
candidates.video_description: Tarrare was an 18th-century Frenchman whose appetite was so extreme it baffled military doctors and horrified an entire nation. He ate cats, snakes, and things far worse — and science still can't fully explain why. One of history's most disturbing medical mysteries.
candidates.script: A French soldier once ate a live cat in front of army doctors — and that was considered one of his milder acts. Tarrare, born around 1772, consumed entire baskets of apples, dozens of raw eggs, and living snakes. His body temperature ran so high that steam rose off his skin. Surgeons studied him for months and had no explanation. When a hospital infant went missing, staff pointed directly at him. No one could prove it. No one could rule it out.

candidates.teaser: There is a language on Earth so complex that linguists say the human mouth may be reaching the absolute limit of what it can physically produce.
candidates.video_title: The Hardest Language the Human Mouth Can Make
candidates.video_description: Taa, spoken by a small community in southern Africa, contains over 100 distinct click sounds — more phonemes than any other known language on Earth. Linguists believe it may represent the very ceiling of human vocal complexity. It could also be one of the oldest languages ever spoken.
candidates.script: One language on Earth has over 100 different click sounds — and getting even one wrong changes the meaning entirely. It's called Taa, spoken by fewer than 3,000 people in Botswana and Namibia. Linguists believe it may be among the oldest languages still spoken, possibly tracing back to the very first humans. It contains more distinct sounds than any language ever recorded. Some researchers think Taa is the closest thing we have to humanity's original voice. Does that change how you see language?

candidates.teaser: For decades, scientists have tracked a whale calling out across the entire Pacific Ocean — and not a single other whale has ever responded.
candidates.video_title: The Whale No Other Whale Can Hear
candidates.video_description: Since 1989, researchers have followed a whale that calls at 52 hertz — a frequency no other known whale species uses. It travels the Pacific alone, singing into silence. Scientists have never seen it, never identified its species, and no whale has ever answered.
candidates.script: Since 1989, a whale has been crossing the Pacific Ocean calling out at a frequency no other whale on Earth uses. Every known species communicates between 10 and 39 hertz. This one calls at 52. Scientists have tracked it for over 30 years using underwater microphones. They've never seen it. They don't know what species it is. And in all that time, not a single whale has ever called back. It has been singing into silence for longer than most people have been alive.

candidates.topic: NASA's Golden Record — Message Hurled Into Deep Space
candidates.teaser: In 1977, NASA launched a golden disc into space containing the sounds of Earth — and it's now so far away that light itself takes over 22 hours to reach it.
candidates.video_title: NASA Sent Earth's Sounds Into Deep Space
candidates.video_description: The Voyager Golden Record, launched in 1977, carries music, greetings in 55 languages, and the sound of a mother's first kiss to her newborn — all encoded on a gold-plated copper disc. Voyager 1 is now in interstellar space. If anyone finds it, they'll know we existed.
candidates.script: In 1977, NASA engraved the sounds of Earth onto a golden disc and fired it into deep space — knowing it would almost certainly never be found. It holds 115 images, greetings in 55 languages, music from Bach to Chuck Berry, and the sound of a mother kissing her newborn child for the first time. Voyager 1 is now 24 billion kilometers away. If an alien civilization finds it in a million years, they will know humans once existed. Does that comfort you, or terrify you?

candidates.topic: The Body Farm — Where Scientists Let Humans Decompose
candidates.teaser: There are facilities in the United States where human bodies are left outside, in the open, on purpose — and what researchers learn there has solved hundreds of murders.
candidates.video_title: The Field Where Human Bodies Are Left to Rot
candidates.video_description: The University of Tennessee's Forensic Anthropology Center — known as the Body Farm — uses donated human remains placed in outdoor environments to study decomposition. The data collected has transformed forensic science and helped convict killers for decades. It's morbid, methodical, and completely essential.
candidates.script: There is a fenced field in Tennessee where human bodies are left outside, uncovered, in every weather condition — and it's one of the most important scientific facilities in America. It's called the Body Farm, opened in 1981 by anthropologist William Bass. Researchers study exactly how the human body breaks down, day by day, season by season. That data has given prosecutors precise time-of-death evidence in hundreds of murder trials. Over 2,000 people have already donated their bodies to go there. Would you?
